# Attempted build-and-test of the candidate fix commit for #5080

Per the skill's guidance ("if the exact commit matters, build it"), an attempt was made to
build the candidate fix commit and its first parent from detached worktrees and run the
issue's repro against both, to confirm the parent fails and the commit does not.

## Candidate

`git log --oneline v1.8.2403.2..v1.8.2405 -- tools/clang/lib/SPIRV/LowerTypeVisitor.cpp`
returns 4 commits; one of them,
`1e59ce9185485535011e1f706d1ab3c1b349eac1` ("[SPIR-V] Fix debug instruction with cbuffer +
FXC (#6531)"), removes exactly the assert quoted in the issue body:

```
- assert(isa<SpirvDebugGlobalVariable>(debugInstruction) &&
-        isa<HybridType>(debugSpirvType));
+ assert(isa<SpirvDebugGlobalVariable>(debugInstruction));
+ if (isa<HybridType>(debugSpirvType)) { ... } else {
+   debugInstruction->setDebugSpirvType(debugSpirvType);
+ }
```

and its commit message explains the trigger as "the requested constant buffer layout is
DX" -- i.e. `-fvk-use-dx-layout`, which matches s-perron's own comment ("the test case
passes if you remove -fvk-use-dx-layout"). Its parent is `690ec7cd7d8d2bc685c8ded6e5f2f932b4a88909`.
Both commits' `external/` submodule tree is identical
(`git ls-tree <sha> external` is `33596a7559cc3f4406c5c8c56ca1cd0097b794f3` for both), so the
only source difference between the two arms is this commit's own 3-file diff.

## What was tried, and why it was abandoned

Two detached worktrees were created outside this repository
(`<repo>\..\dxc-5080-parent`, `<repo>\..\dxc-5080-fix`), each initialising its own submodules
from the same pinned commits, per the skill's "outside the repository working tree and in
separate build directories" instruction. Neither touched the shared `main-debug` build
directory or its ground-truth target.

Configuring either worktree with the machine's only available CMake (4.3.1, bundled with
Visual Studio 18) failed immediately: `CMakeLists.txt:26`'s
`cmake_policy(SET CMP0051 OLD)` errors with "this version of CMake no longer supports it."
The *current* `main` tree (registered as `main-debug`) no longer contains that
`if (POLICY CMP0051) ... endif()` block at all -- so `main` has already independently made
the same forward-compatibility change this verification needed. Removing the identical
4-line block from both worktrees' `CMakeLists.txt` (a build-system-only policy directive,
not compiler logic, applied identically to both arms) let configuration succeed.

Building then failed on a second, unrelated toolchain-drift problem: dozens of translation
units in `external/SPIRV-Tools` and `lib/Transforms/*` failed under `/WX` with
`warning C5285: cannot declare a specialization for 'std::is_nothrow_constructible':
Specializing this standard library template is forbidden by N5014 [meta.rqmts]/4`, raised
from `include/llvm/ADT/StringRef.h` against the installed MSVC 14.51 standard library. This
is a compiler/standard-library version mismatch between the ~18-month-old commit and today's
toolchain, unrelated to the defect under test, and it recurs across enough files that
suppressing it safely (rather than silently disabling `/WX` wholesale, which could mask a
real warning) was judged not to be a small, targeted, identically-applied fix like the CMake
policy change was.

Continuing down this path would mean carrying a second, larger, less obviously-neutral patch
into both build arms purely to satisfy modern-toolchain drift. Given the cost was no longer
"cheap next to the claim," the attempt was abandoned in favour of the release-level bisection
(v1.8.2403.2 crashes, v1.8.2405 clean -- see `out-v1.8.2403.2.txt`, `out-v1.8.2405.txt`) plus
the literal source-diff match above. Both worktrees were removed
(`git worktree remove --force`) without being built to completion; no artifact from this
attempt was published, and nothing outside `data/issues/5080/` was touched.

**Conclusion:** the fix attribution to `1e59ce9185485535011e1f706d1ab3c1b349eac1` is
*strong, not certain* -- based on an exact quoted-assert match in the diff and a two-release
bisection window, not on a direct built-binary before/after comparison.
